name: memory-augmented-run
description: Cross-run memory, modeled the sammy-pack way: memory is a SOURCE you read at the start of a run and write at the end, backed by the durable memory store at /api/memory/:key. Wiring: GET /api/memory/<key> → pass its `content` as the `memory` input → run → PUT /api/memory/<key> with the final output (the updated store). memory-reader surfaces only the prior learnings relevant to this task; memory-writer emits the deduped, pruned updated store. This is what makes a system compound — it stops starting cold — and it's the durable home for the calibration/override feedback the reactive flows generate.

inputs.name: memory
inputs.description: The durable memory store from prior runs (learnings, decisions, known issues, corrections). Empty on the first run. Wire it from a file / DB / Notion / any source; the final phase emits the updated store to persist back.

phases.name: recall
phases.description: Read memory at the start — surface ONLY the prior learnings relevant to this task (scoped recall, not the whole store).

phases.name: work
phases.description: Do the task, informed by hindsight rather than starting cold.

phases.name: persist
phases.description: Write back at the end — emit the UPDATED memory store (append any durable lesson, dedupe, prune stale). Persist this output to your memory source so the NEXT run starts warmer.
